key_insight: Different flow-matching paths can produce the exact same objective yet lead to very different SGD variance and convergence rates, so path choice is an optimization lever, not just a modeling detail.
engineering_relevance: For scalable generative modeling, selecting or learning a variance-reducing path can lower training cost and improve convergence without changing the target FM problem.
method: Analyzed gradient variance across the class of paths that preserve the same marginal distributions and velocity field.
Derived a tight SGD iteration-complexity bound for a 1D Gaussian linear model and identified an optimal linear path.
Formulated PathOpt_θ with constraints that preserve the FM objective and showed how to rewrite them using sample-estimable quantities.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports supporting experiments on Gaussian data, Gaussian mixture models, and real datasets, validating the theory empirically.
watch_item: Variance reduction alone is not sufficient; paths must satisfy the same-marginal constraint G(p_t, v_t^*) or convergence can get worse.
paper_title: Same Flow, Different Paths: Variance Reduction in Flow Matching
